'''Umberto Colombo''' (1927 &ndash; 13 May 2006) was an Italian chemical engineer, academic and the minister of universities, science and technology of Italy.

==Early life and education==
Colombo was born in 1927.<ref name=colombo>{{cite journal|author1=U. Colombo|author2=D. Siniscalco|title=Environmental economics and sustainable development|journal=Dimensions of Sustainable Development|volume=II|url=http://www.eolss.net/Sample-Chapters/C13/E1-46B-20.pdf}}</ref> He received a PhD in [[physical chemistry]] from the [[University of Pavia]].<ref name=colombo/><ref name=leadpro/> He was a Fulbright Fellow at [[the Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in the United States.<ref name=leadpro/>

==Career==
Colombo trained as a chemical engineer <ref name=front3april>{{cite journal|title=Bose's microwave transmitter|journal=Frontline|date=21 March – 3 April 1998|volume=15|issue=6|url=http://www.frontline.in/navigation/?type=static&page=flonnet&rdurl=fl1506/15060810.htm}}</ref> and worked as a professor at the [[University of Milan]] in the 1970s.<ref>{{cite news|author=Jeffrey Hart|title=No good news, please|date=15 February 1977
|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=TydHAAAAIBAJ&pg=4868,2055382&dq=umberto+colombo&hl=en|access-date=25 April 2013|newspaper=Lewiston Evening Journal}}</ref> He served as the president of the Italian energy firm [[Eni]] for a short period from November 1982 to January 1983 <ref>{{cite book|title=Cuando el mercado se estremece: el reto directivo de la reestructuración de la industria|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=m_NjfG-dpyEC&pg=PA155|year=1986|page=155|publisher=Harvard Business Press|isbn=978-0-87584-136-6}}</ref> before being appointed as the head of the Italian nuclear energy unit.<ref>{{cite news|title=Energy Chief In Italy Quits|access-date=25 April 2013|agency=Reuters|location=Rome
|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1983/01/27/business/energy-chief-in-italy-quits.html|newspaper=The New York Times|date=26 January 1983}}</ref>

From 1993 to 1994 Colombo served as the minister of universities, science and technology in the [[Ciampi Cabinet|Ciampi cabinet]].<ref name=prnews26june>{{cite news|title=ECD names a new board member|url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/ECD+NAMES+A+NEW+BOARD+MEMBER-a017138986|access-date=25 April 2013|work=PR News|date=26 June 1995|archive-date=5 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305065853/http://www.thefreelibrary.com/ECD+NAMES+A+NEW+BOARD+MEMBER-a017138986|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Dan V. Segre|title=The Roles of the Jews in Italian Society|journal=Jerusalem Center for Public Affairs|date=17 January 2010|issue=53|url=http://jcpa.org/article/the-roles-of-the-jews-in-italian-society/}}</ref> Following this he became a member of the Italian national council of economy and labour.<ref name="front3april"/> He was one of the shareholders of Energy Conversion Devices and became a member of its board of directors in July 1995 before retiring in November 2004.<ref name=pr24may>{{cite news|url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/Umberto+Colombo,+Former+ECD+Director,+Dies+in+Rome,+Italy.-a0146161876|title=Umberto Colombo, Former ECD Director, Dies in Rome, Italy|date=24 May 2006|work=PR News|access-date=25 April 2013|archive-date=15 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160315223635/http://www.thefreelibrary.com/Umberto+Colombo%2c+Former+ECD+Director%2c+Dies+in+Rome%2c+Italy.-a0146161876|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Other posts that Colombo held included the chairman of [[ENEA (Italy)|ENEA]] (Italian national agency for new technology, energy and the environment; 1983-1993), president of the [[European Science Foundation]] (1991-1993), chairman of the Italian hydrocarbons trust, director general of Montedision's R&D and strategic planning, director of Montecatini's G. Donegani research centre, governor of the international development research centre (IDRC; 1985-1990) in Canada, chairman of [[the United Nations]]'s advisory committee on science and technology for development (1984-1986), chairman of LEAD-Europe,<ref>{{cite journal|author=Valentina Sereni|date=September–October 1998|title=No Simple Recipe|url=http://server11.infn.it/pub/galileo/galileo_eng/archivio/doss/9810/2_art.html|journal=Galileo|archive-date=4 March 2016|access-date=25 April 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304033804/http://server11.infn.it/pub/galileo/galileo_eng/archivio/doss/9810/2_art.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> and president of the European institute research management association.<ref name=colombo/><ref name=leadpro>{{cite web|title=Umberto Colombo Profile Page|work=Lead|access-date=25 April 2013|url=http://www.lead.org/component/comprofiler/userprofile/BDIT0008}}</ref><ref name=prnews26june/><ref name=pr24may/> He was also a member of the [[Club of Rome]]'s executive committee that had been founded by [[Aurelio Peccei]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Declaration of the Club of Rome|url=http://www.mega.nu/ampp/cor.html|work=The Club of Rome|access-date=31 May 2013|archive-date=20 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150720214937/https://www.mega.nu/ampp/cor.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Works===
In 1989, Colombo and fellow Italian scientist Francesco Scaramuzzi experimented with [[nuclear fusion]], reporting that they had successfully created nuclear fusion at room temperature.<ref>{{cite news|date=19 April 1989|newspaper=Lawrence Journal|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=mE4yAAAAIBAJ&pg=6328,4893169&dq=umberto+colombo&hl=en|title=Italian gets nuclear fusion with new technique|access-date=25 April 2013
|agency=[[Associated Press]]|location=Rome}}</ref>

===Awards===
Colombo was the recipient of the Honda Foundation's award for ecotechnology in 1984.<ref name=colombo/><ref>{{cite web|title=Past Laureates, 1980|url=http://www.hondafoundation.jp/en/project/hondaprize/list1980.html|work=Honda Foundation|access-date=18 July 2013|url-status=dead
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131005060617/http://www.hondafoundation.jp/en/project/hondaprize/list1980.html|archive-date=5 October 2013}}</ref> He was also awarded China's state international scientific and technological cooperation award in 1999.<ref>{{cite news|title=China Confers State Award to Brazilian Expert|url=http://english.people.com.cn/english/200006/28/eng20000628_44133.html|access-date=18 July 2013
|newspaper=[[People's Daily]]|date=28 June 2000}}</ref>

==Death==
Colombo died in Rome on 13 May 2006, aged 78.<ref name=pr24may/>
